docs.guide.env.summary: Use a typed contract for build-time environment files generated by the Angular CLI schematic.
docs.guide.env.contract: BaseEnvironment requires readonly production and version fields; add application-specific fields in your own interface.
docs.guide.env.buildTime: Angular replaces the selected environment file during the build. Values included in a browser bundle are public, so do not store secrets there.
docs.guide.env.schematic: Run ng add @rivinia/env in an Angular CLI workspace to scaffold environment files and build replacements.
docs.guide.env.api.baseEnvironment: Type contract for the required production and version properties.
docs.guide.env.api.schematic: CLI schematic that creates environment files and build configuration replacements.
docs.env.installation.title: Installation
docs.env.installation.intro: Install the package in your Angular CLI workspace. It provides a TypeScript contract and an ng-add schematic; it does not load configuration at runtime.
docs.env.scaffolding.title: Scaffolding environments
docs.env.scaffolding.intro: Run the schematic from the workspace root. It asks which environment files and build configurations to create.
docs.env.scaffolding.step.project: For a single-project workspace, the default project is selected. In a multi-project workspace, pass --project <name> to target a specific app.
docs.env.scaffolding.step.environments: Choose dev, stage, and/or prod in the prompt. If no selection is provided, all three are scaffolded; stage also accepts the short build name stag.
docs.env.scaffolding.step.files: The model and base environment file are always created. Stage and production files are created when those environments are selected. Existing files are skipped individually.
docs.env.scaffolding.selectionNote: The schematic also wires the selected build configurations and sets their output folders when no custom outputPath is already configured. It adds /builds to .gitignore when it sets these output folders.
docs.env.configuration.title: Configuration and usage
docs.env.configuration.intro: The schematic wires Angular build configurations to environment files. Import the stable base path in app code; the build replaces that file for stage or production.
docs.env.configuration.contractText: BaseEnvironment requires readonly production and version properties. Add only the fields your application needs to AppEnvironment, then use the same type for each environment file.
docs.env.configuration.filesText: Set the matching API URL and other public settings in environment.ts, environment.staging.ts, and environment.prod.ts. Development uses the base file directly. The schematic snapshots the app package version when it creates these files.
docs.env.configuration.usageText: Always import environment from the base path, never directly from a stage- or production-specific file. Angular selects the right file during the build.
docs.env.configuration.buildText: Use these configuration names after scaffolding. stag is the short configuration name for the staging environment.
docs.env.output.title: Build output folders
docs.env.output.text: The schematic sets an outputPath only when that build configuration does not already define one. The production build goes to builds/prod; staging and development use their own folders. Existing custom output paths are preserved.
docs.env.configuration.customText: If you maintain custom build configurations, ensure each configuration points to the intended file in fileReplacements. The schematic adds missing replacements without removing existing user configuration.
docs.env.configuration.security: Environment files are compiled into the browser bundle. Anyone using the app can inspect those values, so never put secrets or private keys in them.
docs.guide.http.summary: Use one typed client for Observable requests and signal-driven Angular HTTP resources.
docs.guide.http.client: RiviniaHttp delegates to Angular HttpClient, so application interceptors and HttpContext remain available.
docs.guide.http.resource: Use getResource for reactive GET requests; a signal or reactive endpoint can trigger refetching, and undefined disables the request.
docs.guide.http.envelopes: Response bodies pass through by default. Envelope unwrapping and failure validation are opt-in request or provider policies.
docs.guide.http.api.inject: Injects the configured RiviniaHttp client into an Angular service.
docs.guide.http.api.joinUrl: Joins a base URL and endpoint without duplicate slashes; absolute HTTP URLs pass through.
docs.guide.http.api.resource: Creates a reactive GET resource with Angular httpResource state.
docs.http.guidesIndex.title: Choose a guide
docs.http.overview.title: Typed HTTP in two styles
docs.http.quickStart.title: Quick start
docs.http.quickStart.text: Install @rivinia/http, configure the Angular HTTP backend once, then inject RiviniaHttp in an application service. The ng add schematic adds the separate-provider setup to an existing standalone app config.
docs.http.quickStart.note: Requests use the endpoint you pass. Compose an API base URL in your application and use joinUrl when you need to combine path segments.
docs.http.configure.title: Configure the HTTP backend
docs.http.configure.intro: RiviniaHttp wraps Angular HttpClient. Configure the HttpClient backend and RiviniaHttp providers once in app.config.ts. Choose one of the following backend setups.
docs.http.configure.separateText: Use provideHttpClient(...) for Angular features such as interceptors, then provideRiviniaHttp() for the Rivinia client. This is the setup generated by ng add and is useful when you want the Angular backend configuration explicit.
docs.http.configure.featuresText: Pass Angular HttpFeature values through httpFeatures. Rivinia's provider registers provideHttpClient(...) with those features and provides the client configuration.
docs.http.configure.oneText: Choose either the separate provideHttpClient(...) call or the httpFeatures option. Do not use both: that registers the HTTP backend twice and can duplicate the XSRF interceptor.
docs.http.configure.existingTitle: If your app already provides HttpClient
docs.http.configure.existingText: Keep the existing provideHttpClient(...) call and its features. Add provideRiviniaHttp() without httpFeatures so you do not register the backend again.
docs.http.observables.title: Observable requests
docs.http.observables.text: Use the typed methods for GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, and DELETE. They return RxJS Observables and forward Angular HttpClient options such as headers, params, context, and credentials. URLs are passed through unchanged.
docs.http.resources.title: Reactive resources with signals
docs.http.resources.text: getResource uses Angular httpResource for GET requests. A signal or reactive function can drive the endpoint and selected request fields; changing them triggers a new request, while an undefined endpoint disables it. Read value only after hasValue() is true.
docs.http.responses.title: Response envelopes and errors
docs.http.responses.text: Bodies are returned raw by default. Opt into one-level envelope unwrapping per request with unwrap and unwrapKey. Optional envelope policy can detect backend-declared failures before unwrapping; errors flow through the Observable error channel or resource.error().
docs.http.testing.title: Testing HTTP requests
docs.http.testing.text: Provide Angular's HTTP testing backend after provideHttpClient(), then verify the outgoing request and flush a response. This keeps RiviniaHttp on the same testing path as HttpClient.
docs.http.api.title: Public API
docs.http.api.intro: Use these tables as the working reference for the exported providers, common jobs, HTTP methods, and TypeScript option shapes. The examples use Trip and TripDraft as application-owned types.
docs.http.api.requestOptionsText: params, headers, context, withCredentials, and envelope are shared request options. params accepts HttpParams or a primitive-valued object. Request methods pass the URL and options to Angular HttpClient; they do not prepend a base URL.
docs.http.api.resourceText: getResource uses Angular httpResource. Endpoint, params, headers, and context may be reactive inputs; other options are read when the resource is created. Use hasValue() before reading value().
docs.http.api.envelopesText: Unwrapping is opt-in per call and requires both unwrap: true and a non-empty unwrapKey. It extracts one own property. A configured envelope policy checks the raw response first; false success throws RiviniaHttpEnvelopeError.
docs.http.api.providerRow: Provides optional envelope configuration. httpFeatures also registers HttpClient features; use it instead of a separate provideHttpClient() call.
docs.http.api.clientRow: Typed Observable methods plus a reactive GET resource API; it owns no base URL or backend policy.
docs.http.api.job.url: Joins the supplied base and endpoint, collapsing repeated boundary slashes. Absolute HTTP URLs pass through.
docs.http.api.job.unwrap: Strict one-level extraction. A missing key or non-object body throws RiviniaHttpUnwrapError.
docs.http.api.job.resource: Creates an Angular httpResource with Rivinia envelope, unwrap, and parse behavior.
docs.http.api.job.state: Read value only when hasValue() is true; use error(), isLoading(), progress(), and reload() as needed.
docs.http.api.shape.config: Global httpFeatures and optional envelope policy. There is no global unwrap setting.
docs.http.api.shape.request: Shared request fields plus a discriminated union: unwrap: true requires unwrapKey; when unwrap is off, unwrapKey is forbidden.
docs.http.api.shape.raw: Request fields for raw methods; unwrap options are rejected.
docs.http.api.shape.delete: DELETE request options add an optional body and the same unwrap contract.
docs.http.api.shape.resource: Reactive request fields include params, headers, context, parse, defaultValue, reportProgress, and envelope.
docs.http.api.shape.envelope: Configurable successKey, errorKey, and throwOnFailure policy; defaults use isSuccess and error.
docs.http.api.shape.errors: Typed errors expose the raw body and, for envelope failures, the failure code.
docs.http.api.client: Typed Angular HTTP methods and reactive GET resources.
docs.http.api.provider: Provides optional envelope configuration and can configure HttpClient when httpFeatures are supplied.
docs.http.api.envelopeError: Error raised for a failed configured response envelope.
docs.http.api.unwrapError: Error raised when the requested response key cannot be extracted.

docs.http.changelog.1.0.4: Updated published internal dependency metadata and version-pinned documentation links for the synchronized Rivinia 1.0 patch. No public API changes.
docs.guide.theme.summary: Set semantic CSS custom properties once so Rivinia components share the same palette and color scheme.
docs.guide.theme.tokens: Map tokens such as --rv-bg, --rv-fg, and --rv-accent in the application's global stylesheet.
docs.guide.theme.schemes: The stylesheet includes light and dark values; data-rv-theme on the document element selects a scheme.
docs.guide.theme.adapters: Choose one base stylesheet or stack adapter. An adapter includes the base theme, so importing both duplicates CSS.
docs.guide.theme.api.base: Base stylesheet with the default semantic tokens for Rivinia components.
docs.guide.theme.api.css: Explicit stylesheet entry point for bundlers that need a file path.
docs.guide.theme.api.adapters: Tailwind, Bootstrap, and Sass adapter entry points for existing styling stacks.
docs.theme.overview.title: Overview
docs.theme.overview.description: One semantic CSS token layer for Rivinia component colors, surfaces, shape, and type.
docs.theme.contract.title: A CSS contract, not an Angular service
docs.theme.contract.body: @rivinia/theme ships stylesheets and tokens. It exports no Angular providers, runtime manager, or components; import one stylesheet globally and customize its public --rv-* properties.
docs.theme.cascade.title: How values reach components
docs.theme.cascade.body: A component-specific token falls back to its semantic token, then to the component's own built-in value. Theme defaults are inside @layer rivinia-theme, so ordinary unlayered application CSS overrides them regardless of import order.
docs.theme.quick-start.title: Quick start
docs.theme.quick-start.description: Install the stylesheet, import it globally, and set your palette once.
docs.theme.install.title: Install
docs.theme.install.body: Add the package to the Angular workspace. It has no Angular peer dependency; tslib is listed as a package dependency.
docs.theme.import.title: Import globally and set a palette
docs.theme.import.body: Put the import and root tokens in the application's global stylesheet. A bare package import requires a bundler that resolves CSS exports; without one, use the explicit theme.css entry.
docs.theme.guides.title: Guides
docs.theme.guides.description: Choose a focused guide for palettes, schemes, scoped values, framework adapters, or accessibility.
docs.theme.guide-map.title: Choose a theme guide
docs.theme.guide-map.body: Customize your theme explains the cascade; Light, dark and system covers the document scheme; Scoped themes shows subtree overrides. Tailwind, Bootstrap, Sass and Less each have separate integration steps, followed by accessibility and contrast guidance.
docs.theme.guides.customize.title: Customize your theme
docs.theme.guides.customize.description: Set global semantic tokens and understand component fallback behavior.
docs.theme.customize.global.title: Set semantic tokens globally
docs.theme.customize.global.body: Define public tokens in a global stylesheet such as src/styles.css. Start with the background, foreground, and accent; add the remaining tokens only when you need to change them.
docs.theme.customize.fallback.title: Component tokens and fallbacks
docs.theme.customize.fallback.body: Components can expose more specific tokens such as --rv-select-bg. Those resolve through the corresponding semantic token (here --rv-bg), then the component's built-in fallback. A component-specific value set on :root still takes precedence over a semantic value set only on a nested subtree.
docs.theme.guides.schemes.title: Light, dark and system
docs.theme.guides.schemes.description: Use the OS preference by default or explicitly select a document color scheme.
docs.theme.schemes.contract.title: Choose the document scheme
docs.theme.schemes.contract.body: With no attribute, the stylesheet follows prefers-color-scheme. On the root html element, data-rv-theme=light forces light and data-rv-theme=dark forces dark. Remove the attribute to return to system preference.
docs.theme.schemes.bootstrap.title: When Bootstrap owns the switch
docs.theme.schemes.bootstrap.body: The Bootstrap adapter maps theme values to Bootstrap variables and follows data-bs-theme. In that adapter, data-rv-theme does not switch the mapped Bootstrap palette. A switch button and persistence are application behavior; this package does not provide a theme manager.
docs.theme.guides.scoped.title: Scoped themes
docs.theme.guides.scoped.description: Apply semantic tokens to a subtree without changing the document-wide scheme.
docs.theme.scoped.title: Override tokens on a subtree
docs.theme.scoped.body: Set semantic properties on a wrapper to theme the Rivinia components beneath it. The data-rv-theme scheme attribute is read on html, not arbitrary subtrees; use token overrides and set color-scheme yourself if native controls in that subtree need it. In Angular, put global :root rules in a global stylesheet because component style encapsulation prevents them from targeting the document root.
docs.theme.guides.tailwind.title: Tailwind CSS v4
docs.theme.guides.tailwind.description: Add the adapter and use generated color utilities while customizing --rv-* tokens.
docs.theme.tailwind.import.title: Import the Tailwind adapter
docs.theme.tailwind.import.body: Import Tailwind first, then the Rivinia adapter. The adapter includes the base theme, so do not also import @rivinia/theme.
docs.theme.tailwind.utilities.title: Use utilities and customize at the source token
docs.theme.tailwind.utilities.body: The adapter registers bg-rv-bg, text-rv-accent, border-rv-border and related utilities through @theme inline. Change --rv-* properties on the element or an ancestor. Do not use --color-rv-* as the customization API: those are generated aliases, and replacing one can sever its link to the semantic token.
docs.theme.guides.bootstrap.title: Bootstrap 5.3
docs.theme.guides.bootstrap.description: Map Bootstrap's palette to Rivinia and let data-bs-theme control both.
docs.theme.bootstrap.import.title: Import Bootstrap and the adapter
docs.theme.bootstrap.import.body: The Rivinia adapter includes the base theme. Import it once alongside Bootstrap; the shown order is recommended for readability.
docs.theme.bootstrap.switch.title: Let Bootstrap own the color mode
docs.theme.bootstrap.switch.body: The adapter maps Rivinia semantic colors to Bootstrap 5.3 variables and supports data-bs-theme=light or dark. Bootstrap has no matching shadow variable, so Rivinia keeps its own shadow value.
docs.theme.guides.sass-less.title: Sass and Less
docs.theme.guides.sass-less.description: Use the published Sass entry with Sass tooling or the explicit CSS file from Less.
docs.theme.sass.title: Sass / SCSS
docs.theme.sass.body: Bundlers resolve the package export for Sass. The Sass CLI needs the Node package importer (Dart Sass 1.71 or newer) and the pkg: specifier shown in its example.
docs.theme.less.title: Less
docs.theme.less.body: Use the explicit CSS file with Less's CSS import mode. The package root resolves to an empty JavaScript module in tooling that ignores CSS exports; the SCSS entry is not a Less file.
docs.theme.guides.accessibility.title: Accessibility and contrast
docs.theme.guides.accessibility.descript: Understand documented contrast targets and native forced-colors behavior.
docs.theme.accessibility.contrast.title: Contrast targets and limits
docs.theme.accessibility.contrast.body: The documented default text pairs (foreground, muted, and accent on the background) meet 4.5:1 in both schemes. Status colors are checked at 3:1 for indicators, not as text. Borders are not guaranteed as the only control boundary. Recheck contrast after changing tokens; framework custom palettes are outside these default measurements.
docs.theme.accessibility.forced.title: Forced colors
docs.theme.accessibility.forced.body: Some Rivinia components define forced-colors styles in their own packages. The theme stylesheet does not replace those component rules; test interactive states with the actual component and system high-contrast settings.
docs.theme.api.title: API
docs.theme.api.description: Public stylesheet entry points and the twelve semantic CSS custom properties.
docs.theme.api.tokens.title: Semantic token reference
docs.theme.api.tokens.body: These are the twelve public tokens. Color values are light / dark; non-color values are shared unless specified.
docs.theme.token.radius: Default corner radius: 0.625rem in both schemes.
docs.theme.token.font: System font stack: system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif.
docs.theme.api.entries.title: Package entry points
docs.theme.api.entries.body: Choose one entry per application. Tailwind and Bootstrap adapters include the base stylesheet; importing an adapter and the base together duplicates the theme CSS.
docs.theme.entry.base: Package root; its style export resolves to the base theme stylesheet in CSS-aware bundlers.
docs.theme.entry.css: Explicit path to the base theme stylesheet.
docs.theme.entry.tailwind: Base theme plus Tailwind CSS v4 @theme inline mappings.
docs.theme.entry.bootstrap: Base theme plus Bootstrap 5.3 variable mappings.
docs.theme.entry.scss: Sass module that forwards the theme stylesheet.
docs.theme.changelog.title: Changelog
docs.theme.changelog.104.body: Updates published internal dependency metadata and version-pinned documentation links for the synchronized Rivinia 1.0 patch. No public API changes.
docs.theme.changelog.100.body: First stable release of the semantic CSS token system, stylesheet adapters, and light/dark theme contract.
docs.guide.menu.summary: Build accessible action menus with a ready-made UI or the headless menu controller.
docs.guide.menu.actions: Use this menu-button pattern for actions. It is not a navigation menubar or a general-purpose listbox.
docs.guide.menu.keyboard: The UI supports arrow navigation, typeahead, Escape to close and restore trigger focus, and Tab to leave the menu without trapping focus.
docs.guide.menu.layers: The UI entry provides rendering and keyboard/focus behavior. The headless entry tracks menu state and items while your application owns markup and semantics.
docs.guide.menu.api.controller: Headless controller for open state, item registration, active item, and keyboard movement.
docs.guide.menu.api.component: Ready-made menu component with declarative items or projected menu rows.
docs.guide.menu.api.trigger: Marks the trigger element and emits the selected item's id after the menu closes.
docs.guide.popup.summary: Use shared headless helpers to position popup panels and attach dismissal listeners.
docs.guide.popup.position: Calculate viewport coordinates from trigger and panel geometry, placement, and text direction; the result reports when vertical placement flips.
docs.guide.popup.dismissal: Bind outside-pointer, scroll, and resize dismissal for an open popup. Angular DestroyRef cleans up listeners; null browser objects are safe.
docs.guide.popup.boundary: This package provides no markup, styles, open state, focus policy, keyboard handling, or row semantics; the host component owns those decisions.
docs.guide.popup.api.position: Calculates clamped popup coordinates for the supplied geometry and placement.
docs.guide.popup.api.dismissal: Registers dismissal listeners and cleans them up with the host lifecycle.
docs.guide.popup.api.constants: Default trigger gap and viewport edge inset used by the positioning helper.
docs.guide.select.summary: Choose between the headless selection controller and the ready-made select field; both use the same single- or multi-value model.
docs.guide.select.modes: Single mode selects one value and closes. Multiple mode toggles values and keeps the list open so the user can continue selecting.
docs.guide.select.filtering: Search filtering is case- and accent-insensitive and normalizes Arabic tashkeel, tatweel, and alef forms.
docs.guide.select.forms: The ready-made component implements Angular FormValueControl and works with Signal Forms, Reactive Forms, and ngModel.
docs.guide.select.api.controller: Headless registry, filter, and selected-value controller.
docs.guide.select.api.component: Ready-made field that renders the popup, options, and keyboard/focus behavior.
docs.guide.select.api.change: Value type emitted by the UI; its shape depends on single or multiple mode.
docs.guide.datepicker.summary: Select civil Gregorian dates or date-times with optional UI, locale formatting, keyboard navigation, and explicit time-zone handling.
docs.guide.datepicker.civilValues: RiviniaDate and RiviniaDateTime represent calendar values; time-zone conversion is an explicit operation rather than an implicit Date conversion.
docs.guide.datepicker.timeZones: Use the time-zone helpers to resolve wall time and daylight-saving ambiguity for a named zone.
docs.guide.datepicker.locale: Locale controls date/time formatting, hour cycle, labels, and direction; the UI supports RTL and Angular forms.
docs.guide.datepicker.api.values: Civil date and date-time value types accepted by the controller and UI.
docs.guide.datepicker.api.controller: Headless calendar state and navigation controller.
docs.guide.datepicker.api.components: Ready-made date-only and date-time form controls from the UI entry point.
docs.guide.table.summary: Model typed rows and columns with a headless signal pipeline, then render them with the optional grid UI or custom markup.
docs.guide.table.typedColumns: Define columns against the row type so accessors, cell values, and table state stay connected to your data model.
docs.guide.table.pipeline: The core includes search, filters, sorting, pagination, row selection, and row/column span calculations.
docs.guide.table.customization: Use the ready-made grid to render the model, or keep the controller and render custom table markup.
docs.guide.table.api.create: Creates the reactive table model from signal-backed column and data options.
docs.guide.table.api.column: Builds a typed column definition and accessor.
docs.guide.table.api.paginate: Returns the requested page and paging metadata for rows.
docs.guide.modal.summary: Open typed modal content and receive typed results while configuring admission, dismissal, and lifecycle policies.
docs.guide.modal.typedResults: Pass a data type when opening a modal and receive a result that distinguishes confirmed, dismissed, and other completion states.
docs.guide.modal.guards: Async guards can prevent dismissal, allowing unsaved changes or validation to be handled before the modal closes.
docs.guide.modal.admission: Choose stack or queue admission for multiple modals; the optional UI host handles dialog rendering and positioning.
docs.guide.modal.api.provider: Registers the modal manager and its lifecycle configuration.
docs.guide.modal.api.open: Opens typed content with data, a stable reference, metadata, and dismissal options.
docs.guide.modal.api.result: Handle for awaiting a typed modal completion result.
docs.guide.toast.summary: Queue transient notifications through a signal-based service and render them with the optional toast-list UI.
docs.guide.toast.queue: The service manages toast state, timers, deduplication, and overflow independently from how notifications are rendered.
docs.guide.toast.actions: A toast may include an action; choose a kind and duration that fit the message and allow users enough time to respond.
docs.guide.toast.layers: Use the service headlessly when needed, or render the managed list component from the separate UI entry point.
docs.guide.toast.api.inject: Injects the toast service into an Angular component or service.
docs.guide.toast.api.show: Adds a configured notification to the managed queue.
docs.guide.toast.api.list: Renders and manages visible notifications from the UI entry point.
docs.guide.toast.reference.headless: Use the service without the UI

home.pillar.performance.text: Separate headless and UI entry points are marked side-effect free, which supports tree-shaking.
home.pillar.accessibility.title: Accessibility
home.pillar.accessibility.text: Ready-made UIs document keyboard and ARIA behavior; headless usage leaves markup and focus decisions to you.
docs.i18n.overview.title: @rivinia/i18n
docs.i18n.overview.description: A signal-based language manager for dictionaries, ICU messages, direction and locale, with optional language controls.
docs.i18n.entry-points.title: Choose an entry point
docs.i18n.entry-points.body: The core renders no UI. Import each optional control from its own entry point. The UI and select exports are Experimental in 1.0.4.
docs.i18n.entry-points.row.0: Providers, manager, translation pipe, ICU and loaders.
docs.i18n.entry-points.row.2: Language picker; requires the optional @rivinia/select peer.
docs.i18n.language-flow.title: How the pieces fit
docs.i18n.language-flow.body: Register languages once, load dictionaries, then read messages with t(), translate() or rvTranslate. A language switch updates reactive text, document direction and locale formatting.
docs.i18n.quick-start.title: Quick start
docs.i18n.quick-start.description: Install, generate a typed language module, register it and render your first translation.
docs.i18n.installation.title: Install
docs.i18n.installation.body: Requires Angular ^22.0.0. Install @rivinia/select only when using the picker entry point.
docs.i18n.scaffolding.title: Generate the language module
docs.i18n.scaffolding.body: Run init from the workspace root. It writes src/app/i18n/languages.ts and empty dictionaries in public/i18n. Existing dictionaries are preserved.
docs.i18n.register-provider.title: Register once at bootstrap
docs.i18n.register-provider.body: The generated module exports i18n and injectI18n. i18n.provide() loads the initial dictionary before first paint by default.
docs.i18n.first-dictionary.title: Add translation keys
docs.i18n.first-dictionary.body: Put the corresponding Arabic messages in public/i18n/ar.json using the same keys. Nested objects and literal dotted keys are supported.
docs.i18n.first-translation.title: Render and switch
docs.i18n.first-translation.body: Import RvTranslatePipe into the component. Create t() signals once as fields, and call them in the template.
docs.i18n.guides.title: Guides
docs.i18n.guides.description: Choose a task: translate text, configure dictionaries, switch languages or build a language control.
docs.i18n.choose-a-guide.title: Choose a guide
docs.i18n.choose-a-guide.body: Each guide covers one responsibility with working code and the relevant contracts.
docs.i18n.guides/translating.title: Translating text
docs.i18n.guides/translating.description: Choose between signals, immediate translation calls and the template pipe.
docs.i18n.translation-methods.title: t(), translate() and rvTranslate
docs.i18n.translation-methods.body: t() returns a computed Signal<string>. translate() returns the string for the current state. The impure pipe delegates to translate(); prefer pre-created signals for long lists.
docs.i18n.translation-methods.row.0: Use for component fields; a params callback tracks the signals it reads.
docs.i18n.translation-methods.row.1: Use in ordinary TypeScript; store the result only when a snapshot is intended.
docs.i18n.translation-methods.row.2: Import RvTranslatePipe and use it in a template expression.
docs.i18n.reactive-parameters.title: Reactive message parameters
docs.i18n.reactive-parameters.body: Create t() once. Changing either count or the active language recomputes this message.
docs.i18n.default-values.title: Default text and inline maps
docs.i18n.default-values.body: defaultValue is a per-message fallback after the current and fallback dictionaries. An explicit default prevents missing-key reporting. Inline maps resolve current language, fallback language, first value, then an empty string.
docs.i18n.pipe-usage.title: Template pipe
docs.i18n.pipe-usage.body: The pipe accepts a key, optional default text and parameters, or an inline map. Pass localized text to controls yourself.
docs.i18n.guides/configuration.title: Configuration and dictionaries
docs.i18n.guides/configuration.descripti: Configure languages, defaults, dictionary sources and server rendering.
docs.i18n.language-contract.title: Language metadata
docs.i18n.language-contract.body: id selects the dictionary; nativeName labels controls; dir is required; locale drives Intl and ICU. Use ar-EG when Arabic-Indic digits are desired. defaultLanguage is the initial choice when no stored preference or browser match wins. fallbackLanguage supplies missing messages.
docs.i18n.dictionary-loaders.title: Choose a loader
docs.i18n.dictionary-loaders.body: jsonLoader() reads i18n/{language}.json relative to the application base. The built-in loaders use fetch. httpLoader and remoteLoader are lazy; jsonLoader is available during initialization.
docs.i18n.inline-dictionaries.title: Inline dictionaries and preload
docs.i18n.inline-dictionaries.body: translations seeds dictionaries; a later loader response wins. preload defaults to true. For an inline-only application, use a custom loader returning an empty object to avoid network requests. ready() marks initial readiness; isLoading() marks active loading.
docs.i18n.server-rendering.title: SSR and hydration
docs.i18n.server-rendering.body: The default loader resolves absolute URLs from REQUEST and the document base. Dictionaries transfer through TransferState. Custom SSR hosts must provide REQUEST and serialize the application TransferState. Cookie storage can preserve the server language; local and session storage cannot be read on the server.
docs.i18n.guides/switching.title: Language switching and locale
docs.i18n.guides/switching.description: Control language changes, document direction, persistence and formatting.
docs.i18n.switch-language.title: Immediate and awaited switching
docs.i18n.switch-language.body: setLanguage() follows switchStrategy: instant flips first, preload-first waits for the dictionary. setLanguageAsync() waits and keeps the previous language on failure. It resolves without throwing; inspect currentLanguage and loadingError to confirm the result.
docs.i18n.language-signals.title: Read language state
docs.i18n.language-signals.body: languages, currentLanguage, currentLanguageObject, dir, isRtl, locale, ready, loadingState and loadingError are readonly signals. autoApplyDirection keeps html lang and dir synchronized; lang uses the locale.
docs.i18n.persistence-detection.title: Remember and detect the language
docs.i18n.persistence-detection.body: A stored preference wins over browser detection; detection wins over defaultLanguage when enabled. persist defaults to true and records explicit switches, not initial selection. storageStrategy supports local, session, cookie and none.
docs.i18n.locale-formatting.title: Format numbers and dates
docs.i18n.locale-formatting.body: Formatting follows locale(). Create a computed value when a stored label must update with a language change. View-transition configuration is Experimental and feature-detected.
docs.i18n.guides/icu.title: ICU messages
docs.i18n.guides/icu.description: Keep grammatical choices and locale formatting inside the translated message.
docs.i18n.plural-messages.title: Plural and exact matches
docs.i18n.plural-messages.body: ICU uses Intl.PluralRules for the dictionary locale. Arabic supports zero, one, two, few, many and other. Use =0 for an exact empty state across languages. # renders the count using the locale.
docs.i18n.select-and-ordinal.title: Select, ordinal and offsets
docs.i18n.select-and-ordinal.body: select chooses a named branch; selectordinal uses ordinal plural rules. With offset:1, =N compares the raw count while categories and # use count minus one. select in ICU is message syntax, separate from the language picker component.
docs.i18n.icu-formatting.title: Numbers, dates and unsupported syntax
docs.i18n.icu-formatting.body: Supported number styles are percent, integer and ::currency/XXX; date styles are short, medium, long and full. Missing parameters and malformed constructs remain visible as raw placeholders. formatIcu() exposes the same formatter outside dictionaries.
docs.i18n.guides/resilience.title: Fallback and recovery
docs.i18n.guides/resilience.description: Handle missing keys, absent parameters and dictionary failures.
docs.i18n.resolution-order.title: Message resolution order
docs.i18n.resolution-order.body: Key lookup checks the current dictionary, fallback dictionary, explicit defaultValue, then the key itself. Fallback messages use their own locale, so an English plural keeps English rules inside an Arabic page.
docs.i18n.missing-reporting.title: Report missing content
docs.i18n.missing-reporting.body: onMissingKey is deduplicated per key; onMissingParam per key/parameter pair. Missing parameters keep their placeholder. Dev warnings are enabled by default unless a handler owns reporting. clearMissingKeys() and clearMissingParams() reset deduplication.
docs.i18n.reload-dictionaries.title: Reload after failure or a deploy
docs.i18n.reload-dictionaries.body: reload() refreshes current and fallback dictionaries and drops other cached languages. reload(id) refreshes one language. Visible content stays while revalidating. Failures resolve false and appear in loadingError/onLoadError; RiviniaLoadError carries url, status and language.
docs.i18n.guides/controls.title: Language controls
docs.i18n.guides/controls.description: Choose a two-language toggle or a multi-language picker. Both optional entry points are Experimental.
docs.i18n.language-toggle.title: Toggle for two languages
docs.i18n.language-toggle.body: Import from @rivinia/i18n/ui. The button displays the destination language. With manager it waits for setLanguageAsync and emits languageChange only when the requested id is confirmed. With languages/current it is presentational and emits synchronously.
docs.i18n.language-picker.title: Picker for several languages
docs.i18n.language-picker.body: Install @rivinia/select and import RiviniaLanguageSelect from @rivinia/i18n/select. It displays the current language. Managed mode owns languages/current/busy; presentational mode receives those inputs and emits a synchronous languageChange.
docs.i18n.control-contracts.title: Labels, busy state and customization
docs.i18n.control-contracts.body: Translate control labels in the application. Toggle requires exactly two languages; use the picker for larger lists. The toggle supports a custom icon and rvLanguageTrigger template. The picker supports search labels, variants and languageSelectOptions(). Core and /ui do not import @rivinia/select.
docs.i18n.guides/cli.title: CLI and typed keys
docs.i18n.guides/cli.description: Generate setup files and check dictionary consistency in CI.
docs.i18n.ng-add.title: Provider schematic
docs.i18n.ng-add.body: ng add inserts a provideRiviniaI18n call into a recognized workspace. It accepts languages, detectBrowser and project options. The optional @angular-devkit/schematics peer is needed for this workflow. init separately generates a typed module and dictionaries.
docs.i18n.typed-keys.title: Generate translation key types
docs.i18n.typed-keys.body: Keys accept strings until the generated declaration augments RiviniaI18nKeyRegistry. The CLI flattens nested objects, sorts keys and uses string leaves only. --check fails when the declaration is stale.
docs.i18n.dictionary-parity.title: Check language parity
docs.i18n.dictionary-parity.body: --parity reports missing/extra keys and missing ICU parameters relative to the base language. Mismatches exit with code 1. init preserves existing dictionaries and protects handwritten modules unless --force is supplied.
docs.i18n.api.title: API
docs.i18n.api.description: Public providers, methods, signals and contracts, grouped by responsibility.
docs.i18n.providers.title: Providers and configuration
docs.i18n.providers.body: Register one configuration at application bootstrap. defineRiviniaI18n preserves the language union and returns config, provide and inject helpers.
docs.i18n.providers.row.0: EnvironmentProviders; initialize the manager at bootstrap.
docs.i18n.providers.row.3: id, optional nativeName, required dir, optional locale.
docs.i18n.translation-api.title: Translation methods
docs.i18n.translation-api.body: Key methods share dictionary resolution and ICU formatting.
docs.i18n.translation-api.row.3: Signal<string>; params can be a reactive callback.
docs.i18n.translation-api.row.4: Signal<string>; reactive message with explicit fallback.
docs.i18n.state-and-actions.title: State and actions
docs.i18n.state-and-actions.body: State is exposed as readonly signals. Switching, dictionary loads and report resets use methods.
docs.i18n.state-and-actions.row.2: Initialization readiness and dictionary request state.
docs.i18n.state-and-actions.row.4: void; first two languages / whole-list cycling.
docs.i18n.loader-contracts.title: Loader and reporting contracts
docs.i18n.loader-contracts.body: Loaders return dictionaries; callbacks report errors without turning failed loads into rejected promises.
docs.i18n.loader-contracts.row.4: key, language, optional fallbackLanguage / key, param, language.
docs.i18n.changelog.title: Changelog
docs.i18n.release-1-0-4.body: Updated published internal dependency metadata and version-pinned documentation links. No public API changes.
